# Recurring Occurrence Lifecycle Checklist: Retroactive Expense Editing and Recurring Transactions

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality (completeness, clarity,
consistency, measurability) of the recurring-template/occurrence lifecycle,
the most novel and highest-risk part of this feature, as a formal gate
before `/speckit-implement`.
**Created**: 2026-09-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [data-model.md](../data-model.md) | [research.md](../research.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist`
command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality
review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the
requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and
satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is
complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the occurrence due-date anchor rule (which day of the week,
      month, or year a template recurs on) documented in spec.md itself,
      rather than only in research.md/data-model.md? [Completeness, Gap,
      Spec §FR-010, §FR-011]. Resolved (Clarifications, this session):
      formalized as FR-011a.
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what a user is told, at template
      creation time, about which specific date(s) it will recur on?
      [Completeness, Gap, Spec §US4]. Resolved (Clarifications, this
      session): FR-010b requires a recurrence-pattern label on each
      template's row after creation, not a separate creation-time preview.
- [x] CHK003 Is a maximum number of active recurring templates per user
      specified, or is "no maximum" an explicit decision rather than a
      silent gap? [Completeness, Gap]. Resolved: no maximum, added as an
      explicit Assumption cross-referencing plan.md's existing scale note.
- [x] CHK004 Is it specified whether a canceled template, and its history of
      confirmed/skipped occurrences, remains visible anywhere after
      cancellation, or disappears entirely from the user's view?
      [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-015]. Resolved (Clarifications, this
      session): disappears entirely, formalized as FR-015b.
- [x] CHK005 Is "a canceled template cannot be reactivated" stated as a
      testable functional requirement, or only as an Assumptions-section
      note with no corresponding MUST-level requirement? [Completeness,
      Traceability, Spec §Assumptions]. Resolved: elevated to FR-015a.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "on each visit" in FR-011 defined precisely enough to
      determine which specific request(s) trigger pending-occurrence
      computation (any authenticated request, or only a request to
      `/recurring`)? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011]. Resolved
      (Clarifications, this session): scoped explicitly to `/recurring`
      and its occurrence-action routes only.
- [x] CHK007 For a weekly or yearly template, is the very first occurrence's
      due date (the creation date itself, or one interval after it)
      unambiguous from FR-011's wording? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011].
      Resolved (Clarifications, this session): first occurrence is the
      creation date itself, now stated explicitly in FR-011a.
- [x] CHK008 Is it specified whether an expense created from a confirmed or
      adjusted occurrence carries any user-visible indication of its
      recurring origin, or does FR-017's "identically to a manually entered
      expense" mean no indication at all? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017]
      Resolved (Clarifications, this session): yes, a visual indicator is
      required (FR-017a); totals/comparisons remain identical regardless.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK009 Does the Key Entities description of Recurring Occurrence
      ("has a status of pending, confirmed, or skipped") read consistently
      with the data model's actual treatment of "pending" as the absence of
      a row rather than a stored status value? [Consistency, Conflict, Spec
      §Key Entities, data-model.md §RecurringOccurrenceAction]. Resolved:
      reworded to state pending is a computed state, not stored.
- [x] CHK010 Do FR-012, FR-013, and User Story 4's acceptance scenarios use
      the three occurrence-outcome terms (confirm, adjust-and-add, skip)
      consistently, with no scenario implying a fourth or different
      outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013, §US4]. Verified: spot
      checked every usage; only grammatical inflections of the same three
      terms appear, no fourth/different outcome introduced. No change
      needed.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for two recurring templates coexisting
      with identical amount, category, and frequency, versus being
      deduplicated or warned against? [Coverage, Gap]. Resolved: added as
      an edge case, both allowed to coexist.
- [x] CHK012 Is behavior specified for a pending occurrence's adjust form
      that was already open when its template got edited (FR-014),
      submitted afterward with now-stale template context? [Coverage, Edge
      Case, Gap]. Resolved: added as an edge case; no conflict exists since
      adjust-and-add validates only the submitted values, not the
      template's current ones.
- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for two concurrent requests
      confirming/adjusting/skipping the same (template, due-date) pair at
      the same time? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap]. Resolved: added as an edge
      case, backed by the existing data-model unique constraint.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK014 Is SC-005's "across the next 3 calendar months" paired with a
      defined verification method that doesn't require literally waiting 3
      months, or left unspecified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]. Resolved:
      added a verification-method note to SC-005.
- [x] CHK015 Does any success criterion measure the recurring feature's
      actual value (for example, time saved versus manual re-entry), or are
      SC-005/SC-006 purely behavioral/existence checks? [Coverage, Spec
      §Success Criteria]. Resolved (decided not to add one): documented in
      Assumptions, consistent with the SC-006 precedent of avoiding
      non-code-testable qualitative UX metrics.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK016 Is the creation-date-as-anchor decision (research.md) traceable
      to any spec-level requirement, or is it purely a planning-phase
      interpretation with no spec-level basis? [Traceability, research.md
      §Occurrence due-date anchor]. Resolved (Clarifications, this
      session): now a spec-level requirement, FR-011a, matching research.md.
- [x] CHK017 Is the assumption that occurrence computation runs
      synchronously on every relevant request (no caching/precomputation)
      validated against any stated scale expectation for a user with many
      active templates? [Assumption, Gap]. Resolved: already covered by
      plan.md § Scale/Scope (low tens per user, no pagination needed); no
      new content required, cross-referenced from spec.md's Assumptions.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality
  criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction,
  or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must
  not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle
  maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
